title: Label tree semantic losses for rich multi-class medical image segmentation
mechanism: Tree-based losses (Wasserstein over a label tree, hierarchy-weighted top-level supervision) penalise confusions by tree distance.
evidence: R: consistent improvements over task baselines on whole-brain parcellation (full labels) and neurosurgical hyperspectral imaging (sparse labels).
adaptation: Same 2-level EL tree as HSSN; loss-only change so confusing gridline with busbar costs less than with background; cheaper than HSSN, run first.
min_experiment: Arm house + Wasserstein tree loss; baseline house; metrics gridline/splice/edge_dark IoU and mIoU_rob; kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01 and splice still 0.
prior_overlap: none; Dice-on-12-classes in section 5 is a different loss
